transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2027-01-23
Start time: 10:00 AM PST
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Ortiz (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Leo Park (Redwood CSM), Carlos Mendes (Azimuth CTO), Rina Shah (Azimuth ML), Tom Varela (Azimuth Infra)

Summary: Quick discovery to understand Azimuth's search/reranking stack, vector DB preferences, throughput SLOs, dimensionality question for embeddings, and security constraints for pilot.

--- Auto-generated sections (may be imperfect) ---
Topics: embeddings, reranking, vector DB, dedicated capacity, VPC/KMS, hybrid search
Action Items (auto): see action_items field

Transcript:
[00:00] Jamie: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro — I'm Jamie, AE on the inference team at Redwood, with Priya our solutions eng. how's everyone doing?
[00:08] Carlos: good thanks. Carlos here. we're excited — been poking at a few options for embeddings + rerank, mostly to speed up our QA search.
[00:15] Priya: great. can you give us a quick picture of your current infra and what you hope to get out of a rerank flow?
[00:21] Rina: sure — currently we index docs in Postgres + Elastic for the lexical stuff, embeddings are stored in Pinecone for a couple of experiments. we do a BM25 step in Elastic to get a candidate set (~100), then vector similarity to narrow, then a reranker model to rescore top 10.
[00:38] Tom: infra constraints — everything runs in our AWS account. data residency in us-west. we'd prefer either a VPC private deployment or dedicated capacity with VPC peering. hosts are a no-go for raw doc storage.
[00:48] Jamie: totally — that's helpful. so you're doing hybrid search already (BM25 + vector) which is pretty typical. quick Q — what's your 95th percentile latency target for search end-to-end?
[00:56] Carlos: under 200ms ideally for the user-facing call. at peak traffic, we can see 250 rps across all endpoints but search is maybe 60 rps.
[01:06] Priya: ok that clarifies. for a pipeline that does Elastic candidate fetch (50ms), vector nearest neighbor (depends on DB), and reranker model call (the big one) — we can provide hosted API paths if you care more about quick time to value, or Dedicated clusters if you need predictable throughput and private networking.
[01:22] Rina: curious on vector DB options — we leaned on Pinecone but worried about cost and dimensionality (their perf seems to hit a wall at 1536 dims). we also looked at Milvus but worried about ops overhead. does Redwood have recommendations?
[01:32] Priya: we often see customers use either hosted vector DBs (Pinecone, Weaviate managed) or self-hosted Milvus/FAISS inside Dedicated/Private deployments. Redwood doesn't force a particular vector store — we have connectors for the common ones and can run the vector similarity inside our runtime too — if you want to avoid a separate vectorDB, we can do the ANN step as part of the Redwood serving flow (this speeds the loop but has tradeoffs for persistence and scaling).
[01:55] Tom: interesting. so you can host embeddings and ANN in your runtime? how about scaling to 250 rps and maintaining <200ms?
[02:03] Priya: depends on the model and dimensionality. for 768-dim embeddings and approximate nearest neighbor (HNSW) we can reach pretty high qps on Dedicated; for 1536 or 3072 dims the index is heavier and requires more memory and tuned sharding. we recommend profiling a sample of your corpus. that's why the pilot will run a hosted and dedicated variant so we can show numbers.
[02:25] Carlos: what's your recommended embedding dim? our current production model is 1024 dims from an open model — curious if we should downsize to 768 or up to 1536 to improve reranker performance.
[02:33] Jamie: short answer — it depends on your use case. embedding dimensionality tradeoffs: higher dims can marginally help recall but cost memory and index time, also vector DB cost. many customers find 768 or 1024 sweet spots for QA search; 1536+ is common for multi-modal or fine-grained semantic similarity. the reranker downstream effect is also important — often a smaller embedding with stronger reranker gives better practical results than massive dimensions.
[02:55] Rina: gotcha. also what about embedding model choice? we tried an off-the-shelf open model but the vectors don't align well with our reranker. any guidance?
[03:03] Priya: we can recommend models — Redwood hosts a few verified embedding models and we provide profile metrics like throughput (embeds/sec), cost/token, and vector quality on benchmark sets. we'll share the embedding model comparison sheet. often we run a calibration set to see nearest neighbor precision@k and then check end-to-end rerank MRR.
[03:22] Tom: security — you mentioned KMS and audit logs. we'd need customer-managed keys (HSM/KMS) for production. plus SOC2 evidence. can Dedicated or Private do that?
[03:31] Leo: yeah I can take that — Redwood Dedicated supports VPC peering and can be configured with customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest. Private (on-prem/VPC) gives you full control. we also have SOC2 Type II and ISO attestation — I'll share the pack.
[03:43] Carlos: and data retention — we can't keep user content for longer than 30 days in the hosted product, otherwise it must be isolated; is that configurable?
[03:50] Jamie: yes, retention policies are configurable for Dedicated/Private. Hosted has default retention windows and options — we'll send the retention matrix.
[03:57] Rina: about reranker model latency — what are realistic numbers for a small transformer reranker? our current reranker is a 2-layer cross-encoder fine-tuned for QA.
[04:05] Priya: cross-encoder latency depends on sequence lengths and batch sizing. for short sequences (question + doc snippet) a small cross-encoder (like a distilled model) can be ~15-40ms on a GPU per request with batching; on CPU it's much slower. Redwood Dedicated can give you guaranteed concurrency and batching to get stable p95s. also we support async rerank pipelines where you return a fast approximate result and fill in a better rerank after.
[04:31] Tom: what's the unit economics — e.g., token vs embedding cost — we need to model cost for 60 rps sustained.
[04:38] Jamie: we'll provide a TCO sheet. quick rule: embeddings cost is per-vector compute and storage; rerank cost is the big one if you're doing many cross-encoder calls. Dedicated amortizes GPU costs, lowering per-call cost for heavy workloads.
[04:51] Carlos: integration effort — how much work to swap out Pinecone for Redwood-managed vector or connector?
[04:57] Priya: for connectors we have out-of-the-box integrations for Pinecone, Milvus, Weaviate, and you can plug in a S3 + FAISS workflow. migration usually involves exporting vectors and reindexing; for the runtime ANN we can accept your embedding stream or generate embeddings in Redwood and persist them in your chosen store. we'll share a migration checklist.
[05:18] Rina: any advice on index type? HNSW vs IVF?
[05:22] Priya: HNSW is commonly preferred for recall/latency sweet spot for static indexes. IVF + PQ can help with huge corpora where memory is the limiting factor. We'll help pick parameters based on your corpus size, dims, and qps.
[05:35] Carlos: curious about real numbers — can you give sample latencies from customers?
[05:39] Jamie: from our benchmarks — small FAQ-style corpora with 768 dims and HNSW on Dedicated hit ~50ms p95 for ANN queries; cross-encoder rerank end-to-end to re-score top10 can add 20-60ms depending on model. Hosted API numbers are similar but less predictable under noisy multi-tenant peaks.
[05:58] Tom: for the pilot, we'd like both hosted (fast path) and dedicated (predictable path) runs — and compare P95 and cost.
[06:06] Priya: perfect. we'll stand up a dedicated benchmark run and a hosted variant using your sample. please note hosted will have retention defaults; if you require KMS/VPC we should do Dedicated or Private.
[06:17] Carlos: timeline — we want a POC in two weeks if possible.
[06:20] Jamie: doable if you can get the sample dataset up by Friday. Priya — can you prepare the benchmark template now?
[06:25] Priya: yes — I'll send template and an example S3 presigned link for upload.
[06:29] Rina: thanks. one more Q — how does Redwood handle updates to vector indexes (frequent writes)? our corpus is updated hourly with new docs.
[06:36] Priya: incremental updates are supported. for high write rates we recommend a hybrid approach — a small in-memory write buffer for recent docs plus periodic merges into the main ANN index; Dedicated gives you control over memory and refresh intervals. We'll include guidance in the checklist.
[06:50] Tom: any gotchas integrating with our infra (VPC peering, EKS, SAML SSO)?
[06:55] Leo: we support SAML/SSO and role-based access controls; for VPC peering we do a brief networking workshop to exchange CIDRs and peering flows. EKS customers commonly run the Private bundle if they want on-prem style control.
[07:08] Carlos: thanks, that's helpful.
[07:12] Jamie: quick recap — action items: we (Redwood) will send pricing/TCO, security pack, benchmark template; Azimuth will upload sample corpus and confirm whether Dedicated or Private is required for the pilot. we'll aim to run hosted + dedicated benchmarks within the next week.
[07:27] Rina: sounds good. we'll aim to upload data by 2027-01-29.
[07:31] Jamie: great — thanks everyone. we'll follow up with calendar invites for the technical deep dive next week.
[07:36] Carlos: thanks all. bye.

End of transcript.
